title: Virid Salis
subtitle: Scraped from oxidized copper
text: Copper left to the open air grows a green crust — verdigris, the old alchemists called it. Salt and time and moisture working together against the metal. An Unstained with a brush can harvest this accretion. Take any unwaxed copper that has weathered at least one step — exposed, weathered, or fully oxidized — and brush it. The patina flakes away, the copper returns one step toward bright, and what falls into your hand is Virid Salis: a green salt-ash that carries the virtue of that long slow cleansing. Waxed copper will not yield it. The wax has sealed the process. Only copper that has been allowed to change is useful here. A line of Virid Salis laid across a threshold will repel the infected. Monsters that step across it are stung by the salt. Blood constructs and creatures made of corrupted blood suffer worse — slowed and scorched for crossing it. Those who have advanced far enough in the Hematic Order to be called Perfected — the fifth degree and beyond — will feel the salt's censure as well. Their blood has soaked through them too deeply to pass unmarked.
